title: A New Hire's First Week
body:
#new-team-intros

**Sam (Team Lead):** Welcome aboard, Alex! Great to finally have you here. Feel free to drop any questions in this channel — no such thing as a silly one during week one.

**Alex (New Hire):** Thanks Sam! Quick question already — I've got access to the main repo, but I'm not seeing the deployment docs anyone mentioned in onboarding. Am I missing a permission somewhere?

**Sam:** Good catch, that's actually a gap in our onboarding checklist. The deployment docs live in a separate internal wiki that isn't linked from the main repo README. I'll get you added today and flag it so we fix the checklist for the next hire.

**Alex:** No worries, happy to help spot these things. In the meantime, is there someone I should shadow for a deploy, or is it more of a "read the docs and figure it out" situation?

**Sam:** Definitely shadow first — deploys can be nerve-wracking the first time. Priya usually handles Tuesday deploys, I'll ask if she's okay with you sitting in this week.

**Alex:** Sounds great, thank you. I'll hold off on touching the deploy pipeline myself until then.

**Sam:** Appreciate that. And seriously, keep the questions coming — it's much easier to fix a small gap now than to have it trip up the next five people who join.

Wait until the onboarding checklist is rewritten

summaryPrompt: Summarize this conversation in 80-120 words, covering the problem Alex found and how Sam plans to handle it.
responsePrompt: Write a short response as Alex, thanking Sam and asking one more clarifying question about the deploy shadowing session.
